mainTopic: Who must give the מתנות כהונה, how they are enforced, divided and eaten, and which כהנים may receive them.
overview: The amud opens with רב אושעיא finishing an earlier discussion about a בכור that a כהן already received and later sold to a ישראל after it got a blemish. The משנה says that one who slaughters for a כהן or a גוי is exempt from the gifts, and רבא learns from its wording and from a פסוק that the duty falls on the butcher, even a כהן butcher. In a story, רבי טבלא advises a poor כהן to partner with Israelite butchers. רב נחמן still obligates them, because a כהן butcher is exempt only for his first weeks, and not at all once the shop is set up. רב חסדא bans a כהן who withholds the gifts, and the גמרא explains that the twenty-two-year ban on the butchers of הוצל teaches that we may fine them without warning. Next come rules on splitting the gifts between כהנים and on רבי יוחנן's view that the meat is like טבל, which the הלכה rejects. The amud ends with רב חסדא's rules that the gifts are eaten roasted with mustard, and that a כהן must be expert in the twenty-four gifts. That last rule is rejected by a ברייתא about a כהן who does not accept the עבודה, and the ברייתא's list of services continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אושעיא limits the case to a בכור the כהן already received
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא explains that the case being discussed is a בכור that already came to a כהן and was then sold to a ישראל after it got a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: We are talking about a firstborn animal that already came into the hands of a כהן, and then the כהן sold it to a ישראל once it had a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion about a כהן making a claim on an animal. רב אושעיא answers by pointing to a very specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כהן could claim a בכור as his. Here, though, the כהן already received this בכור once. After it got a blemish he sold it to a ישראל, so he cannot come back and demand it again as a firstborn.

keyTerms.meaning: It came into the hands (possession) of a כהן
A blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
A firstborn male animal, which is given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
It is a case where it came into the hands of a priest
phrases.notes: 'It' is the firstborn animal from the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: and he sold it to an Israelite in its blemished state.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised just before this section, on the earlier part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a כהן can always claim the animal as a firstborn.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here he can't, because he already received it once and then sold it in its blemished state.

steps.title: The משנה: slaughtering for a כהן or a גוי is exempt from the gifts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: someone who slaughters an animal for a כהן or for a גוי is exempt from the מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters an animal for a כהן or for a גוי does not have to give the gifts of foreleg, jaw and maw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה so that it can study its wording. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gifts are normally given to a כהן from every animal slaughtered for regular eating. When the animal belongs to a כהן or a גוי, there is no obligation. The משנה phrases this as 'one who slaughters for' them, and that wording will be important.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts: foreleg, jaw and maw, given to a כהן

phrases.english: One who slaughters for the priest and for the gentile
is exempt from the gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering an animal for a כהן or a גוי is exempt from the gifts.

steps.title: Why not simply say the כהן and גוי are exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה used the roundabout phrase 'one who slaughters for' instead of just saying a כהן and a גוי are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה just say: A כהן and a גוי are exempt from the gifts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording, which seems longer than it needs to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the point is only that animals of a כהן or a גוי are exempt, the simple wording would be clearer. The extra mention of 'the one who slaughters' must be teaching something, and the next step explains what.

keyTerms.meaning: But let it teach (why not word it this way?)

phrases.english: But let it teach: A priest and a gentile
are exempt from the gifts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A shorter, simpler wording was available, so why did the משנה use a longer one?

steps.title: רבא: the obligation is on the butcher
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the wording teaches that the כהן collects his claim from the טבח, the one doing the slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches that the claim for the gifts is against the butcher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by showing what the משנה's wording teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By focusing on 'the one who slaughters,' the משנה shows that the duty to give the gifts is on the butcher, not only on the owner. So if a butcher who is himself a כהן slaughters a ישראל's animal, he still has to give the gifts. Only slaughtering an animal that belongs to a כהן or a גוי is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows us (a lesson learned from the wording)
The claim is against the butcher

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a כהן butcher is exempt just because he is a כהן. What matters is whose animal it is, and the obligation is placed on the butcher.
steps.whyThisMatters: It decides who is responsible to give the gifts in practice: the butcher.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is to say,
the claim is with the butcher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the longer wording was needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could have just said a כהן and a גוי are exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording teaches that the obligation is on the butcher, even a כהן butcher.

steps.title: רבא's פסוק: even a כהן butcher must give
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the פסוק that the gifts come 'from the people' and not from the כהנים, yet 'from those who slaughter' includes even a כהן butcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא expounded: 'From the people' means not from the כהנים. But since the פסוק also says 'from those who slaughter,' this tells you that even a butcher who is a כהן is included.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports his rule from step 4 with a דרשה on the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From the people' alone would exempt every כהן. The added words 'from those who slaughter' make the obligation depend on the slaughtering. So a כהן butcher who slaughters a ישראל's animal must give the gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say (this is the only explanation)

steps.whatToRemember: The gifts are not taken from a כהן's own animal. But a כהן who works as a butcher for a ישראל must still give them.

phrases.english: Rava expounded:
"From the people" – and not from the priests;
when it says "from those who perform a slaughter" –

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר אֲפִילּוּ טַבָּח כֹּהֵן בַּמַּשְׁמָע.
phrases.english: you must say that even a butcher who is a priest is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק that supports רבא's rule in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the obligation is on the butcher, even a כהן butcher

steps.title: רבי טבלא's poor כהן host asks for help
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבלא's host was a כהן who was short of money, and he came to רבי טבלא for advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טבלא's host was a כהן, and he was having a hard time making a living. He came to רבי טבלא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to the משנה's rule that an animal partly owned by a כהן is exempt from the gifts. This step sets up the advice in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story only sets the scene here: a כהן in money trouble. The practical solution comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: His host (the person he stayed with)
Things were tight for him (he was short of money)

phrases.english: Rabbi Tavla's host was a priest,
and things were tight for him.
He came before Rabbi Tavla.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a story about the משנה's rule on a partnership with a כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the story: a poor כהן asks רבי טבלא for help.

steps.title: רבי טבלא's advice: partner with ישראל butchers
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבלא tells the כהן to become a partner with Israelite butchers. They will gladly let him in, because his share makes their animals exempt from the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told him: Go become a partner with the Israelite butchers. Since a partnership with you frees them from giving the gifts, they will be happy to take you in as a partner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טבלא gives practical advice that uses the rule that an animal shared with a כהן is exempt from the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal partly owned by a כהן is exempt from the מתנות. The butchers save the cost of the gifts, so they have a reason to take the כהן in as a partner. This gives him a share in their business and a way to earn money.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because of (one thing leads to the other)

steps.whatToRemember: An animal jointly owned with a כהן is exempt from the gifts, and רבי טבלא used this rule to help a poor כהן earn a living.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go and become a partner
with the Israelite butchers,
for since they become exempt from the gifts,
they will partner with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל אִישְׁתַּתַּף בַּהֲדֵי טַבָּחֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the advice that the story in step 6 set up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partnership with a כהן exempts the animals from the gifts, so the butchers have a reason to take the כהן in as a partner.

steps.title: רב נחמן obligates the partnership anyway
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן requires the butcher partnered with the כהן to give the gifts. When the כהן protests that רבי טבלא exempted them, רב נחמן warns him to give them or he will knock down רבי טבלא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן obligated him to give the gifts. He said: But רבי טבלא exempted us! רב נחמן answered: Go and give them out, and if not, I will pull רבי טבלא out of your ear.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the כהן followed רבי טבלא's advice, but רב נחמן still rules that the gifts must be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following the logic of Step 7, a partnership with a כהן should exempt the animals. רב נחמן rejects that result in practice. His sharp warning shows he believes רבי טבלא's ruling cannot be relied on here, and that he has a solid reason, which comes in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman obligated him,
phrases.notes: The כהן had taken רבי טבלא's advice and gone into partnership with Israelite butchers.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא רַבִּי טַבְלָא פַּטְרַן!
phrases.english: He said to him: But Rabbi Tavla exempted us!
He said to him: Go, take them out [and give them],
and if not,
I will take Rabbi Tavla out of your ear.
phrases.notes: He means: I'll knock down the basis for רבי טבלא's ruling, so you can't lean on it anymore.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical result of רבי טבלא's advice, which רב נחמן overrides
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The butcher partnered with a כהן must still give the gifts.

steps.title: רבי טבלא asks רב נחמן for his reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבלא comes to רב נחמן and asks why he ruled against the exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טבלא went before רב נחמן and said to him: What is the reason the Master did this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טבלא challenges רב נחמן's ruling by asking for its source. This sets up רב נחמן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface this is a question, but it works as a challenge. Based on the משנה, a כהן's share should exempt the animal, so רב נחמן's ruling seems to go against it.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master (a respectful way to say 'you')

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַבִּי טַבְלָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Tavla went before Rav Nachman,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא עָבֵיד מָר הָכִי?
phrases.english: and said to him: What is the reason the Master did this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling made in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling obligating the partnership
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts an animal owned in partnership with a כהן, so why obligate the butchers who took a כהן in as a partner?

steps.title: A כהן butcher is exempt only for the first weeks
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites the זקני דרום: a כהן טבח is exempt for two or three weeks, and after that he must give the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When רבי אחא בר חנינא came from the South, he said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the elders of the South said: A כהן who is a butcher is exempt from the gifts for two or three weeks. From then on, he is obligated in the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers with an earlier teaching that limits the exemption of a כהן butcher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption for a כהן is not permanent. Once he has been working as a butcher for more than a few weeks, he is treated like any regular butcher and must give the gifts. So רבי טבלא's trick does not hold up over time.

keyTerms.meaning: a כהן who works as a butcher
the gifts given to a כהן (the foreleg, jaw, and stomach)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the משנה's exemption for a כהן. It limits it in time: the exemption covers only his first few weeks as a butcher.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא מִדָּרוֹמָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: For when Rabbi Acha bar Chanina came from the South,
he said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
that the elders of the South said:
A כהן who is a butcher,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ שַׁבָּתוֹת פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת,
phrases.english: for two or three weeks is exempt from the gifts;
phrases.notes: Here שבתות means weeks, not days of שבת.

phrases.english: from then on, he is obligated in the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא מִדָּרוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי טבלא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Cites a tradition that limits the exemption in time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן butcher, or a partnership with one, is always exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption lasts only two or three weeks. After that, the gifts must be given.

steps.title: Then at least give the first weeks' exemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבלא pushes back: at least follow רבי אחא בר חנינא and exempt the כהן for the first weeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then let the Master at least do for him according to רבי אחא בר חנינא!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טבלא uses רב נחמן's own source against him and asks for the short grace period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כהן butcher is exempt for two or three weeks, this new partnership should also get those weeks free. But רב נחמן obligated them right away, so he seems to go even beyond his own source.

phrases.english: He said to him: Then let the Master do for him
at least according to Rabbi Acha bar Chanina!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן using the source he just quoted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own source grants two or three weeks of exemption, so why not apply it here?

steps.title: The grace period is only before setting up a shop
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that the weeks of exemption apply only to someone who has not yet set up a fixed butcher shop. Here the shop is already set up.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That applies when he has not set up a fixed butcher shop. But here, he has already set up a butcher shop.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers by narrowing when the grace period applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The few free weeks exist because a new כהן butcher is not yet known as a regular butcher. A partnership that joins an already running shop is a fixed business from day one, so the gifts are owed right away.

keyTerms.meaning: set up a fixed butcher shop

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן butcher is exempt only for his first two or three weeks, and not at all if he joins an already established shop. So partnering with a כהן is not a lasting way to avoid the gifts.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּלָא קְבַע מְסַחְתָּא,
phrases.english: He said to him: These words apply where he did not set up a fixed butcher shop,
but here, he has set up a butcher shop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי טבלא's request in Step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every new כהן butcher gets two or three weeks free.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one who has not set up a fixed shop gets the free weeks. An established shop is obligated right away.

steps.title: רב חסדא's ban on withholding the gifts
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא declares that a כהן who does not separate the gifts should be under the ban of the God of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A כהן who does not separate the gifts, let him be under the ban of the God of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins, showing how serious it is not to give the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the previous ruling. A כהן butcher who is obligated, as in Step 10, and still keeps the gifts for himself, is treated very harshly. רב חסדא puts him under a שמתא, a ban.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: This כהן
who does not separate the gifts,
let him be under the ban of the God of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הַאי כָּהֲנָא דְּלָא מַפְרֵישׁ מַתְּנָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement that adds force to the obligation of a כהן butcher
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who withholds the gifts is placed under a ban.

steps.title: The butchers of הוצל under the ban for 22 years
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא reports that the butchers of הוצל had been under רב חסדא's ban for twenty-two years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: These butchers of הוצל have been under the ban of רב חסדא for twenty-two years now.
steps.whatsHappening: A real example of רב חסדא's ban, still in force on a whole town's butchers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the ban was not just a strong statement. It was actually applied and lasted, because those butchers kept refusing to give the gifts.
steps.whatToRemember: Withholding מתנות כהונה is taken very seriously: רב חסדא placed offenders under a ban, and the butchers of הוצל stayed under it for twenty-two years.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
These butchers of Hutzal
have remained under the ban of Rav Chisda
for these twenty-two years now.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי טַבָּחֵי דְּהוּצָל קָיְימִי בְּשַׁמְתָּא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of רב חסדא's ban
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא's ban was actually enforced on the butchers of הוצל for twenty-two years.

steps.title: What practical law comes from the twenty-two years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what law we learn from רבה בר רב שילא's report that the butchers of הוצל were under the ban for twenty-two years.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law was this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבה בר רב שילא bothered to tell us how long the butchers had been under the ban. This question sets up the next steps, where the גמרא will try out answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain report of a fact is not enough. The גמרא wants to know what practical difference the twenty-two years makes for how we treat these butchers now.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What practical difference does this make?
A ban. The person is pushed away from the community until he fixes his ways.

phrases.english: For what law [was this said]?
phrases.notes: He means: why did רבה בר רב שילא tell us they were under the ban for twenty-two years (Step 14)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what law comes out of the report in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law comes from knowing that the butchers of הוצל were under the ban for twenty-two years?

steps.title: Suggestion that the ban now ends is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ban is lifted after twenty-two years, but a ברייתא shows that someone who refuses a מצות עשה is pressured with no limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means we no longer keep them under the ban, there is a problem. A ברייתא teaches: when is this said? For a לא תעשה. But for a מצות עשה, for example, they tell him 'make a סוכה' and he does not, 'take a לולב' and he does not, 'make ציצית' and he does not, then they strike him until his soul leaves him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one answer: after twenty-two years the ban is over. It then knocks that answer down with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving the gifts to a כהן is a מצות עשה. The ברייתא says that when a person refuses a מצות עשה, בית דין keeps pressing with no limit until he does it. So the butchers' ban cannot simply run out after a set time while they still refuse.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This introduces a suggested answer, often one that is about to be rejected.
A positive command, something you must actively do
A prohibition, something you must not do
They strike him until his soul leaves him. בית דין keeps pressing with no limit until he obeys.

steps.confusionAlert: The striking here is not a punishment for a past sin. Its goal is to force the person to do the מצוה now, so it stops the moment he agrees.

phrases.english: If you say that we no longer keep them under the ban,
but it is taught in a ברייתא:
When is this said?
For a prohibition.
But for a positive command,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן אוֹמְרִים לוֹ ״עֲשֵׂה סוּכָּה״ וְאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה,
phrases.english: for example, they tell him 'make a סוכה' and he does not do it,
'[take a] לולב' and he does not do it,
'make ציצית' and he does not do it,
they strike him until his soul leaves him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּתוּ לָא מְשַׁמְּתִינַן לְהוּ וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to Step 15's question and immediately challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that after twenty-two years the butchers are no longer kept under the ban
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For a מצות עשה, בית דין keeps pressing with no limit until the person complies, so a ban cannot simply end with time.

steps.title: It means they may be fined without a warning
steps.stepSummary: The twenty-two years teach that such stubborn people may be fined even without a warning, as רבא and רב נחמן בר יצחק did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means we fine them without a warning. This is like רבא, who fined a man by taking a thigh, and רב נחמן בר יצחק, who fined a man by taking a cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer. Because these butchers have refused for so long, we may fine them right away, with no warning first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The long time under the ban proves that the butchers are stubborn on purpose. So a warning is not needed before fining them. Two stories show this in practice: רבא took a whole thigh, and רב נחמן בר יצחק took a cloak, from people who would not give the gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given before a punishment

steps.whatToRemember: The twenty-two years do not end the ban. They show the butchers are stubborn, so we may fine them without a warning.

phrases.english: Rather, [it means] that we fine them without a warning,
like this case where רבא fined [someone] a thigh,

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק קָנֵיס גְּלִימָא.
phrases.english: [and] רב נחמן בר יצחק fined [someone] a cloak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in Step 16 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The report teaches that people who stubbornly refuse to give the gifts may be fined without a warning.

steps.title: How the three gifts are split among כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that the זרוע goes to one כהן, the קבה to one כהן, and the לחיים may be split between two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: the זרוע goes to one, the קבה to one, and the לחיים to two.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement from רב חסדא about the gifts. He tells us how many כהנים may share each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זרוע and the קבה are each given whole to one כהן. The לחיים (the two jaws) may be split between two כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts given to the כהן from a slaughtered animal
The maw, one of the animal's stomachs

phrases.english: And רב חסדא said:
The foreleg to one [כהן], and the maw to one,
the jaws to two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how the gifts are divided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זרוע goes to one כהן, the קבה to one כהן, and the לחיים may be split between two.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they split every bone
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reported that in ארץ ישראל they split the gifts bone by bone between two כהנים, which seems to go against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But when רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: in the West we divide them bone by bone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. In ארץ ישראל even the זרוע was split between two כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said only the לחיים are split. The report from ארץ ישראל says every gift, bone by bone, was split in two. So it looks like the זרוע and קבה can be split too.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? This introduces a challenge.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר:
phrases.english: But when רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said:
In the West we divide them bone by bone!
phrases.notes: Each bone was split between two כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that the זרוע and קבה each go to only one כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In ארץ ישראל every gift was split between two כהנים, so the זרוע and קבה can be split too.

steps.title: There it was a big ox
steps.stepSummary: The practice in ארץ ישראל was about a big ox, where each part is large enough to split.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it was about an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The splitting in ארץ ישראל was with a big ox, so it does not go against רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a large ox, each gift is big enough that half of it is still a real gift. With a smaller animal it is not, so רב חסדא's rule stands: only the לחיים are split.
steps.whatToRemember: Normally only the לחיים are split between two כהנים. With a large ox, every gift may be split, since each half is still a real gift.

phrases.english: There, [it was] with an ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the report was about a large ox
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In ארץ ישראל all the gifts were split, so every gift may be split in two.
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting every gift applies only to a large ox. For smaller animals, רב חסדא's rule stands.

steps.title: No eating from the animal before its gifts are separated
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: you may not eat from an animal until its gifts are taken off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is forbidden to eat from an animal whose gifts have not been separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי יוחנן. Before the owner eats any of the meat, he must first separate the כהן's gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא discussed how the gifts are given and split. Now it asks a new question: what happens to the rest of the animal before the gifts are separated? רבי יוחנן says the owner may not eat any of it yet.

keyTerms.meaning: was separated / lifted off (used for setting aside a holy portion)
gifts: here the זרוע, לחיים and קבה given to the כהן
an animal (here, a slaughtered ordinary animal)

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is forbidden to eat from an animal
whose gifts have not been separated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָסוּר לֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of splitting the gifts between כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating from an animal before its gifts are separated is forbidden.

steps.title: Eating before separating is like eating untithed food
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן goes further: eating such meat is like eating טבלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who eats from an animal whose gifts were not separated is as if he eats untithed produce.
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement from רבי יוחנן makes the first one stronger. He compares the meat to טבלים, produce that has not yet been tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טבל, the holy portion is mixed into the whole crop, so none of it may be eaten until תרומה and מעשר are taken. רבי יוחנן treats the meat the same way: the כהן's share is 'inside' the animal, so the whole animal is off-limits until the gifts are removed.

keyTerms.meaning: untithed produce, forbidden until תרומה and מעשר are separated
as if; it is treated like

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who eats from an animal
whose gifts have not been separated
is as if he eats untithed produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹכֵל מִבְּהֵמָה שֶׁלֹּא הוּרְמָה מַתְּנוֹתֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens step 21 by comparing the meat to טבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat from an animal whose gifts were not separated has the status of טבל.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that we do not follow רבי יוחנן here.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final ruling: we do not follow רבי יוחנן's strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gifts still must be given, but the rest of the animal is not forbidden like טבל. The comparison to טבלים is rejected for practical הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: the halacha is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: The gifts must still be given, but we do not rule like רבי יוחנן that the meat is like טבל before they are separated.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law: the gifts must still be given, but they are not a holy share that locks up the whole animal.

phrases.english: But the halacha is not like him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on רבי יוחנן's statements in steps 21-22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We do not rule like רבי יוחנן; the meat is not treated like טבל.

steps.title: The gifts are eaten only roasted and with mustard
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a כהן eats the gifts only roasted and with mustard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The gifts of the כהונה are eaten only roasted, and only with mustard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new rule about how the כהן should eat his gifts: roasted, and with mustard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule is not about who gets the gifts. It is about the way they are eaten. The reason comes in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה אֵין נֶאֱכָלוֹת אֶלָּא צָלִי,
phrases.english: The gifts of the priesthood are eaten only roasted,
and they are eaten only with mustard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה אֵין נֶאֱכָלוֹת אֶלָּא צָלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new rule about how the gifts are eaten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gifts must be eaten roasted and with mustard.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רב חסדא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the gifts must be eaten this way. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roasting and mustard sound like oddly specific details. The גמרא wants to know what פסוק or logic stands behind them.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for eating the gifts roasted and with mustard.

steps.title: The gifts were given for greatness, so they are eaten like kings eat
steps.stepSummary: The word למשחה means 'for greatness', so the gifts are eaten the way kings eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'למשחה', which means for greatness: the way kings eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק. The gifts were given to the כהנים as a sign of importance, so they should be eaten in a royal style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word למשחה usually relates to anointing. Here it is read as 'for greatness', since kings are anointed. Kings eat their meat roasted with mustard, so the כהן eats his gifts that way too.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'for anointing'; read here as 'for greatness'

phrases.english: The verse says: 'for prominence'
for greatness, the way that kings eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: למשחה means for greatness, so the gifts are eaten roasted with mustard as kings eat.

steps.title: A כהן who is not an expert in the gifts gets none
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says a כהן who does not know the twenty-four gifts should not be given a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: There are twenty-four gifts of the כהונה. Any כהן who is not an expert in them is not given a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a second rule. Only a כהן who knows the laws of all twenty-four gifts should receive them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule is about who qualifies to receive the gifts. רב חסדא sets a high bar: knowledge of all the laws, not just being a כהן. The גמרא will question this right away.

keyTerms.meaning: the twenty-four gifts given to כהנים

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
There are twenty-four gifts of the priesthood;
any priest who is not an expert in them
is not given a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate statement of רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who is not expert in the twenty-four gifts is not given a gift.

steps.title: Rejected: the real requirement is believing in the עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב חסדא's rule using a ברייתא: a כהן loses his share only if he does not believe in the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is not correct. As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says: Any כהן who does not accept the עבודה has no share in the כהונה, as the פסוק says: 'The one among the sons of אהרן who offers the blood of the שלמים and the fat, he shall have the right thigh as a portion.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רב חסדא's rule is wrong. It brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון sets a different standard: believing in the עבודה, not being an expert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the gift to 'the one who offers', meaning a כהן who accepts the service. So the condition for getting gifts is belief in the עבודה. Nothing requires expertise in all the laws, so רב חסדא's demand is too strict.

keyTerms.meaning: accepts / believes in the Temple service
the right thigh of a קרבן, given to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two standards. רב חסדא wanted expertise. The ברייתא only asks that the כהן believe in the עבודה, and that weaker standard is what the גמרא accepts.

phrases.english: But this is not correct,
as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
Any priest who does not accept the Temple service
has no share in the priesthood's gifts,
as it is said: 'The one who offers the blood of the peace offerings'
and the fat, from among the sons of Aaron,
he shall have the right thigh as a portion.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's rule from step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The requirement that a כהן be an expert in all twenty-four gifts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא makes belief in the עבודה the only condition, not expertise.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא sets a lower standard (belief) for receiving gifts.

steps.title: The ברייתא extends the rule to fifteen more עבודות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the rule covers not only the blood but fifteen other services, and begins to list them.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this one alone. From where do I include fifteen services, such as: the pourings, the mixings, the crumblings, the saltings, the wavings, the bringings near, the removing of handfuls, the burnings, the pinchings...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It says a כהן who rejects any of fifteen other services, not just the blood, also loses his share, and it starts listing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only mentioned blood and fat. The ברייתא widens the rule to many services of מנחות and bird offerings. The list continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (from the פסוק) this case
removing a handful from a מנחה
pinching the neck of a bird offering

phrases.english: I have only this one alone;
from where do we include
fifteen services, such as:
the pourings, and the mixings,
and the crumblings, and the saltings,
the wavings, and the bringings near,
and the removing of handfuls, the burnings,
(and the squeezings), and the pinchings,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'squeezings' (round brackets), but the corrected wording leaves that out and says 'pinchings' (square brackets) instead. The list keeps going after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא זֶה בִּלְבַד, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה עֲבוֹדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 28, expanding its scope.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who rejects any of fifteen additional services also has no share in the gifts.
